newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen ignore rate comment, track JGB rise.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen ignore rate comment, track JGB rise.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures held onto their gains in late Wednesday trade as Japanese government bond (JGB) futures continued to reach for new highs, partly driven by a sharp overnight rise in U.S. treasuries.

Dealers said the market in its current bullish mood, had largely shrugged off a comment by a Japanese Liberal Democratic Party official that the Bank of Japan should raise its official discount rate to 1.0 percent from the current 0.5 percent level.

"News of the comment came around lunchtime but it didn't do much at all," said a Japanese bank dealer, adding that players were quick to buy back the Euroyen futures after an initial nervous reaction.
The lead June Euroyen contract stood at 99.30 in late trade against its IMM close at 99.28. September was at 99.17 against 99.13.
"June should break through its contract high of 99.30 tomorrow...," said the dealer. He said June was still but September was seeing increased interest as it showed further scope for gains.
But dealers said the market would have trouble extending its gains significantly before the U.S. October non-farm payrolls report on Friday.
March Eurodollars finished at 94.46 against their IMM close at 94.43. June were at 94.37 against 94.32. Volume for both months was a relatively healthy 26,500 lots.
December JGBs settled at a new contract high of 125.33 against their previous 124.34.
"We could see a slight correction tomorrow ahead of the Japanese holiday on Monday and the U.S. presidential election on Tuesday," said the dealer.

Eurodollar futures ended sharply higher on follow-through buying after Tuesday's a lower-than-expected third quarter U.S. employment cost index and a drop in the consumer confidence index quelled concerns about inflation.
